clue.text: Vegetable described in a newspaper cutting?

definitions.text: Vegetable described in a newspaper cutting?

parts.words: Vegetable described in a newspaper cutting?
parts.note: a cut-out paragraph from a paper, a '..., split differently names a root vegetable

explanation.walkthrough: In newspaper slang a paragraph is a PAR; a small cut-out of one would be a par snip.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Fruit dishes

explanation.definitionFit: Peaches are stone fruit, and 'peaches' or 'dishes' are both slang for attractive people.

clue.text: Husband substitute?

explanation.definitionFit: To husband is to conserve or keep back, and a reserve is a stand-in player kept on the bench.

clue.text: Railwayman have points to look after

parts.note: NUR, the old National Union of Railwaymen, stands for a railwayman
S and E, south and east, are compass points

explanation.surface: A railway worker is told to keep an eye on the points.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone who is ill is a synonym for looking after them.

clue.text: Has to step out — fast!

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to get going quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of HAS TO STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb meaning with all speed, very quickly.

clue.text: T S Eliot play shows understatement

indicators.note: play suggests the letters frolic about into a new order, as well as a drama

explanation.surface: A production of a T S Eliot drama shows restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun for one of Eliot's dramas but signals an anagram of TSELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the rhetorical figure of ironic understatement, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Drunk started smoking

explanation.definitionFit: Lit up is slang for intoxicated, and also means having set a cigarette alight.

clue.text: Watch and see how long the music takes

parts.note: to time something is to measure how long it lasts
a piece is a single musical composition

explanation.surface: A conductor checks a stopwatch to see how long a performance lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is a small portable clock, a type of timekeeper.

clue.text: Extremely important stations

parts.note: the major stations that sit at the extreme end of the line, where the tracks stop

explanation.definitionFit: Railway stations where lines end are end-of-the-line terminals.

clue.text: Gulpers out to get the whole hog

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Greedy eaters go out to devour an entire pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GULPERS; 'go the whole hog' is an idiom for doing something lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend lavishly is to indulge without restraint, going all the way.

clue.text: Promises certain to be kept by a fool

indicators.note: to be kept by means the word for certain is held inside the word for a fool

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone vows that a simpleton can be trusted to keep something safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge or guarantee something to someone is to give them a firm vow.

clue.text: Many were carried away by it and lost their heads

definitions.text: Many were carried away by it and lost their heads

parts.words: Many were carried away by it and lost their heads
parts.note: reads like people overcome by passion, but describes the cart that took French Revolution victims to the guillotine

explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel was an open cart used to carry the condemned to execution during the Terror.

clue.text: Chastise wanton whores with it

indicators.note: wanton, unruly and undisciplined, signals that the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A stern moralist proposes to punish loose women with a lash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanton' rearranges WHORES into HORSEW; 'with it' then adds HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog with a riding whip is to punish severely.

clue.text: He's good — and early!

explanation.definitionFit: A prior is a monk heading a religious house, a holy man, and prior also means coming before in time.

clue.text: Quiet little person wants place for books

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
an elf is a small fairy-tale being

explanation.surface: A quiet little fellow is after somewhere to keep his books.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge on a bookcase is where volumes are stored.

clue.text: RN fleet manoeuvre entertains mother in port

indicators.note: entertains means hosts, holding the word for mother within
a manoeuvre moves things about, so the letters of RN fleet are rearranged

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A naval exercise welcomes a sailor's mother aboard in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges RNFLEET into FRENTLE, and 'entertains' puts MA inside. Fremantle is the port city of Perth in Western Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fremantle is a harbour city in Western Australia, a seaport.

clue.text: About four hide, being reticent

indicators.note: About here means surrounding, so the word for hide goes around the numeral

parts.note: to secrete is to hide away
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people hide away, keeping quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticent people are reserved and tend to keep things to themselves.

clue.text: Called without once becoming stuck-up

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for called goes around once

parts.note: cited means called, as a witness is cited or summoned

explanation.surface: Someone summoned to court, never once humbled, grows arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, an older sense, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up people are vain and proud of themselves.

clue.text: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on it

definitions.text: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on it

parts.words: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on it
parts.note: the idiom of a new light on a situation, read literally as a lizard whose skin colour shifts with its surroundings

explanation.definitionFit: This lizard alters its skin colour, so a new setting literally changes its look.

clue.text: Author to mark with a tick, say

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, giving a name that sounds like them

parts.note: to check off an item is to tick it on a list

explanation.surface: A writer is told to tick something off.
explanation.walkthrough: Anton Chekhov was the Russian playwright and short-story writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov was a Russian dramatist and short-story writer.

clue.text: Rise for the workers?

parts.note: reads like a pay rise for staff, but is a mound raised by worker insects

explanation.definitionFit: A mound of earth piled up by a colony of insects is a small hillock.

clue.text: No head on the beer, that is strange

indicators.note: No head on means the first letter of beer is taken off

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a pint without froth is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No head on' removes the first letter of BEER, leaving EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird or uncanny feels unsettling.

clue.text: An early caller

parts.note: reads like a dawn visitor, but is the bird that crows at daybreak

explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crows at dawn, waking people early.

clue.text: Train to be articulate

explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast non-stop rail service, and to express a thought is to put it into words.

clue.text: A minor player makes more

explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film walk-on with no lines, and extra means additional.

clue.text: It's not alphabetical, that's obvious, of course

parts.note: clear means obvious
soup is served as one course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a list out of order is plainly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: Alphabet soup contains pasta letters; a consomme has none, so it is not alphabetical.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth without pasta letters in it is the opposite of alphabet soup.

clue.text: Many poems need deciphering

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A heap of verses are so obscure that they must be decoded.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: ciphers are things that need deciphering.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret ciphers are messages written to be decoded by the recipient.

clue.text: Loveless sailor staggers round bars

indicators.note: staggers means reels about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
Loveless means losing the O, love being zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A jilted seaman lurches drunkenly round the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' drops O (love, zero in tennis scoring) from SAILOR, leaving SAILR, which 'staggers' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal rods forming a barrier or rack are bars.

clue.text: Given a lift from this ode

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters of this ode are rebuilt into something new

explanation.surface: A reader is uplifted by a particular poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised up by rope or crane is to be lifted.

clue.text: It gets down to sorting the list

indicators.note: sorting means putting into a new order, so the letters of the list are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone settles down to organise a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting' rearranges THELIST. The definition plays on thistledown, the fluffy seed heads the plant produces.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly weed produces fluffy seed heads known as down.

clue.text: Depressed areas

parts.note: reads like economically deprived regions, but means low-lying land between hills

explanation.definitionFit: Low ground between hills lies sunken below its surroundings.

clue.text: They are said to be just barren areas

definitions.text: They are said to be just

explanation.definitionFit: People get their just deserts, what they merit, and deserts are arid wastelands.
